mainTopic: Rules of נטילת ידים: whole-day stipulation, channel water, valid vessels, the רביעית, and eating with a cloth
overview: The amud opens by finishing רבי אבינא's advice to people short of water: wash once in the morning and make a condition that it covers the whole day. Two versions argue over whether this works only in a שעת הדחק, which decides whether he agrees with רב. רב פפא then rules on washing from a channel filled by buckets. A bucket with a hole joins the channel to the river, so hands may be dipped there, but the bucket itself is useless for pouring. רבא requires a רביעית of water. The גמרא settles two statements of his by saying two people may share water that started as a full רביעית. A second version of אמימר's answer claims the amount does not matter, and the גמרא rejects it, while sages are shown making vessels that hold a רביעית. רבא and a ברייתא rule that a prepared barrel stopper or wineskin is a valid vessel, but a sack or basket is not. Finally the גמרא asks whether one may eat holding food in a cloth instead of washing. A proof from רבי צדוק is rejected, and a new proof from שמואל and רב begins, continuing on the next amud.

steps.title: Wash once in the morning and stipulate for the whole day
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבינא tells the people of the valley of ערבות, who have little water, to wash in the morning and make a condition that it counts for the whole day.
steps.simpleTranslation: To the people of the valley of ערבות: people like you, who don't have much water, should wash your hands in the morning and make a condition that it covers the whole day.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes a ruling that started just before this point. רבי אבינא gives practical advice to people who do not have enough water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One morning washing can count for the whole day if you make a condition on it. The condition is a promise to keep the hands clean all day, so a new washing before each meal is not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Washing the hands (before eating bread)
Morning
Make a condition on them, so the one washing counts for later
A condition or stipulation

phrases.english: [To the people of] the valley of Aravot:

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן אַתּוּן דְּלָא שְׁכִיחִי לְכוּ מַיָּא,
phrases.english: people such as you, for whom water is not readily found,
wash your hands in the morning
and make a condition on them for the whole day.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּגוֹן אַתּוּן דְּלָא שְׁכִיחִי לְכוּ מַיָּא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Where water is scarce, one may wash in the morning and stipulate that it covers the whole day.

steps.title: First version: only when there is a pressing need
steps.stepSummary: One version says רבי אבינא allowed this only in a שעת הדחק. In that case he disagrees with רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: in a time of pressing need, yes; not in a time of pressing need, no. That disagrees with רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first of two ways to understand how far רבי אבינא's permission goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the whole-day condition is only for emergencies, like the water shortage in ערבות. רב allowed it for everyone, so on this reading רבי אבינא argues with רב.

keyTerms.meaning: A time of pressing need, an emergency situation
It disagrees
Yes / no

phrases.english: Some say:
in a time of pressing need, yes,
not in a time of pressing need, no,
and this disagrees with Rav.
phrases.notes: רב had said earlier that anyone may wash in the morning and make a condition for the whole day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבי אבינא's ruling to emergencies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The whole-day condition works only in a time of pressing need, which goes against רב.

steps.title: Second version: even without a pressing need
steps.stepSummary: Another version says רבי אבינא allowed it even with no emergency, so he agrees with רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: even when there is no pressing need it is allowed, and this is the same as רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second way to understand רבי אבינא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this reading, the water shortage was only the reason he happened to give the advice. It was not a requirement. The rule is general, exactly like רב's.

keyTerms.meaning: Also, too
This is the same as רב's view

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions agree that one morning washing with a condition works when water is scarce. They argue only about whether it also works when water is available.

phrases.english: And some say:
even not in a time of pressing need, too,
and this is the same as Rav.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אֲפִילּוּ שֶׁלֹּא בִּשְׁעַת הַדְּחָק נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the opposite reading to step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The whole-day condition works even when there is no pressing need, the same as רב.

steps.title: Washing from an irrigation channel filled by buckets
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that you cannot wash from water flowing in the channel, because no person is pouring it. You can wash right next to the bucket, where the water still comes from a person's pouring.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: with this channel that people fill with buckets, you may not wash your hands from it, because the water does not come from a person's force. But if you bring your hands close to the bucket, so the water comes from a person's force, you may wash from it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching starts. רב פפא explains when water in a man-made channel can be used for נטילת ידים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For washing, the water must reach the hands through a person's act of pouring (כח גברא). Water flowing along the channel moves by itself. Water caught right as it is poured from the bucket still counts as poured by a person.

keyTerms.meaning: A channel or ditch for water
Water-drawers who use buckets
A person's force, meaning the water is poured by a person
Bucket

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule that washing water must come through a person's action, not just flow on its own.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
this channel of the water-drawers,
one may not wash hands from it,
since [the waters] do not come from a person's force.
But if he brings [his hands] close to the bucket,
so that they come from a person's force,
one may wash hands from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הַאי אֲרִיתָּא דְּדַלָּאֵי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Water flowing in the channel cannot be used for washing because no person pours it. Water caught right at the bucket can be used.

steps.title: A bucket with a hole links the channel to the river
steps.stepSummary: If the bucket has a hole big enough to let liquid in, the channel's water counts as joined to the river, so you may dip your hands in the channel.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the bucket has a hole big enough to let liquid in, it joins the waters, and you may immerse your hands in it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא keeps going and adds a new case: a bucket with a hole. This lets the channel be used for dipping (טבילה) instead of pouring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Through the hole, the water in the bucket touches the river, so the channel's water counts as connected to the river. Dipping the hands in it is like dipping them in the river itself, which is a valid way to purify the hands.

keyTerms.meaning: Has a hole, is cracked
A hole big enough for liquid to come in
It joins or links the waters together
Dipping the hands into water instead of pouring

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two methods. Here the hands are dipped into the water (טבילה), not washed by pouring (נטילה). The next step explains why pouring from this bucket would not work.

phrases.english: And if the bucket has a hole
big enough to let liquid in,
it joins [the waters],
phrases.notes: He means the hole links the water in the channel to the river water, as if they were one body of water.

phrases.english: and one may immerse the hands in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a case where the channel water can be used, but by dipping instead of pouring.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bucket with a hole that lets liquid in joins the channel to the river, so hands may be dipped in the channel.

steps.title: A vessel with a hole cannot be used for pouring
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a vessel with a hole big enough to let liquid in may not be used to pour water for washing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: a vessel that has a hole big enough to let liquid in, one may not wash hands from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבא's rule to explain why the bucket with a hole works only for dipping, not for pouring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hole that size means the bucket no longer counts as a proper vessel (כלי). Pouring for washing must be done from a valid vessel, so this bucket cannot be used for pouring.

keyTerms.meaning: Vessel or utensil
Has a hole in it

phrases.english: And Rava said:
a vessel that has a hole big enough to let liquid in,
one may not wash hands from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: כְּלִי שֶׁנִּיקַּב בְּכוֹנֵס מַשְׁקֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the bucket with a hole works for dipping but not for pouring.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vessel with a hole big enough to let liquid in is not valid for washing by pouring.

steps.title: A vessel without a רביעית is not valid
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a vessel that does not have a רביעית of water in it may not be used for washing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: a vessel that does not have a רביעית in it, one may not wash hands from it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new rule of רבא about the minimum amount needed for washing. It also sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording 'אין בו' (does not have in it) points to how much water is actually inside the vessel right now. Pay attention to this wording, because the next step is built on it.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarter-לוג, the minimum amount of water for washing hands
Does not have in it, meaning it is not actually filled

phrases.english: And Rava said:
a vessel that does not have a quarter-log in it,
one may not wash hands from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: כְּלִי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ רְבִיעִית
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not wash from a vessel that does not actually contain a רביעית.

steps.title: Contradiction: what the vessel has in it vs. what it can hold
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this with another statement of רבא, which looks at how much the vessel can hold. That suggests a vessel that can hold a רביעית is fine even if it does not have that much in it now.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רבא said: a vessel that cannot hold a רביעית, one may not wash from it. That means if it can hold a רביעית, it is fine even if it does not have that much in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets two statements of רבא against each other and asks how they fit. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first statement looks at how much water is inside the vessel. The second looks at how much the vessel can hold (מחזיק). The second implies that what counts is the vessel's size, even if less water is in it now, and that seems to go against the first statement.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? An opening word for a challenge
Can hold, has room for
This implies, introducing what follows from a statement
Even though

phrases.english: Is that so?
But didn't Rava say:
a vessel that cannot hold a quarter-log,
one may not wash hands from it,
which implies that if it can hold [a quarter-log],
[it is valid] even though it does not have [that much] in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 7 using another statement of רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that a vessel must actually contain a רביעית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another statement of רבא is about how much the vessel can hold. From it we learn that a vessel that can hold a רביעית is valid even if less water is in it, which goes against step 7.

steps.title: One person versus two people
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the contradiction in רבא. Requiring a רביעית of water actually in the vessel applies when one person washes. Looking at what the vessel can hold applies when two people wash from one original רביעית. A ברייתא supports this.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no contradiction. One statement is about washing for one person, and the other is about washing for two. As a ברייתא teaches: with a רביעית of water you may wash the hands of one person, and even of two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the קשיא from Step 8 by saying each of רבא's statements is about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one person washes, there must really be a רביעית of water in the vessel. If two people wash, the second person may use what is left even though it is less than a רביעית, because the water started out as a full רביעית. The ברייתא saying 'for one, and even for two' backs up this split.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the contradiction goes away
This one... that one...; each statement is about a different case
One may wash the hands (נטילת ידים)

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is for one person, that one is for two,
phrases.notes: The first statement (the water must really be in the vessel) is about one person. The second (what the vessel can hold) is about two.

phrases.english: as it is taught: with a quarter-log of water
one may wash the hands for one person,
and even for two.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא לְחַד, הָא לִתְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (one person vs. two people)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's two statements seemed to disagree about whether the water must actually be in the vessel
steps.terutzMaskana: For one person a real רביעית is needed. Two people can share water that started out as a רביעית.
steps.whatToRemember: A רביעית must start out in the vessel. Once it does, even two people can wash from it.

steps.title: רב ששת asks אמימר what he is careful about
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת asks אמימר whether he is careful about three things: the vessel, the water's appearance, and the amount of water. אמימר answers 'yes' to each one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said to אמימר: Are you careful about the vessel? He said: Yes. About the appearance of the water? He said: Yes. About the amount? He said: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new short discussion. רב ששת checks which washing rules אמימר is careful to keep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three things are basic rules of hand washing. The vessel must be whole. The water must look normal. There must be enough water, a רביעית. In this version אמימר is careful about all three.

keyTerms.meaning: Are you (plural) careful/strict about it?
A vessel; here, a proper whole vessel for washing
Appearance; that the water looks like normal water
The measure; the minimum amount of water

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said to Ameimar:
Are you particular about the vessel?
He said to him: Yes.
About the appearance? He said to him: Yes.
phrases.notes: He means the appearance of the water, that it hasn't changed color or turned murky.

phrases.english: About the measure? He said to him: Yes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת לְאַמֵּימָר: קָפְדִיתוּ אַמָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new exchange about which washing rules are kept in practice
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether אמימר is careful about the vessel, the water's appearance, and the amount of water

steps.title: Another version: not careful about the amount
steps.stepSummary: Some report the answer differently. In this version אמימר is careful about the vessel and the appearance, but not about the amount. He brings the ברייתא that one רביעית can serve one person, and even two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say this is what he answered: We are careful about the vessel and the appearance, but we are not careful about the amount. As a ברייתא teaches: with a רביעית of water you may wash for one person, and even for two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of אמימר's answer. In this version he is lenient about the amount of water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמימר reads the ברייתא to mean the amount does not really matter. After all, two people share one רביעית, so each one gets less than a רביעית. This sets up the גמרא's reply in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: We are careful/strict

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same ברייתא used in Step 9. There it explained רבא, but here it is used to argue that the amount does not matter at all.

phrases.english: Some say, this is what he said to him:
about the vessel and about the appearance, we are particular;
about the measure, we are not particular,
as it is taught: with a quarter-log of water
one may wash the hands for one person,
and even for two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of אמימר's answer to the third question in Step 10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אמימר is careful about the vessel and the appearance, but not about the amount, based on the ברייתא

steps.title: The proof does not work: leftovers of a full רביעית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from the ברייתא. Two people may share only because the second person uses leftovers of water that started as a full רביעית. That does not mean the amount does not matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not correct. The case there is different, because the water comes from the leftovers of an amount that was enough for purity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the second version. It says the ברייתא cannot prove that the amount of water does not matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the water started out as a full רביעית, so the second person is using leftovers of a proper amount. If there was never a רביעית to begin with, even one person may not wash. So the amount does matter.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is not so; the גמרא rejects what was just said
It is different there
Leftovers of purity; what remains from water that started as a full רביעית

steps.whatToRemember: The amount does matter. Water may be shared only if it started as a full רביעית. A vessel that never had a רביעית cannot be used even for one person.
steps.whyThisMatters: This brings us back to the ruling of Step 9. The amount is required, and sharing works only because of the original full רביעית.

phrases.english: But it is not so;
it is different there,
because they come from the leftovers of purity.
phrases.notes: The second person's water is what is left from a full רביעית, which was enough for washing when it started.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof used in the second version of אמימר's answer (Step 11)
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the ברייתא to show the amount of water does not matter
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא is about water that started as a full רביעית, so the shared water is leftover from a proper amount

steps.title: Two sages prepared washing vessels that hold a רביעית
steps.stepSummary: רב יעקב of נהר פקוד and רב אשי in הוצל each prepared a vessel holding a רביעית for washing hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יעקב from נהר פקוד made a washing cup that holds a רביעית. רב אשי in הוצל made a jug that holds a רביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports what two sages actually did: each set up a special vessel that holds a רביעית for washing hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right after rejecting the claim that the amount of water does not matter (step 12), the גמרא shows these sages took care to have a vessel of a full רביעית. Their practice fits the view that a רביעית is needed for washing.

keyTerms.meaning: A washing cup, a vessel used for pouring water on the hands
A small jug
Holding a רביעית (literally 'daughter of a quarter'), the minimum amount for washing
Prepared or set up

phrases.english: Rav Ya'akov from Nehar Pekod prepared
a washing cup that holds a quarter-log;
Rav Ashi in Huzal prepared
a jug that holds a quarter-log.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתְקֵין רַב יַעֲקֹב מִנְּהַר פְּקוֹד נַטְלָא בַּת רְבִיעֵתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof that the amount does not matter was rejected, this report of what the sages practiced supports needing a רביעית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leading sages prepared vessels holding a רביעית for washing, which reflects the rule that a רביעית is required.

steps.title: A prepared barrel stopper may be used for washing
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a barrel stopper that was prepared as a container may be used for נטילת ידים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: if someone prepared a barrel stopper to be a container, he may wash his hands from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new rule about what counts as a vessel for washing: a barrel stopper that was fixed up to hold water is acceptable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A stopper is normally just a lid, not a container. Once someone hollows it out and prepares it to hold water, it becomes a real vessel, so it may be used for washing.

keyTerms.meaning: The stopper or plug of a barrel
That one prepared it, fixing it up to work as a container

phrases.english: And Rava said:
A barrel stopper that one prepared,
phrases.notes: He means it was hollowed out and set up to hold water like a cup.

phrases.english: one may wash hands from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the amount of water to the vessel itself: which objects count as a כלי for washing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A barrel stopper that was prepared as a container is a valid vessel for נטילת ידים.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבא and lists more containers
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same rule about a barrel stopper, adds that prepared leather wineskins are valid, and says a sack or basket is never valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: a barrel stopper that was prepared may be used for washing. Leather wineskins (חמת and כפישה) that were prepared may be used for washing. A sack or a basket may not be used, even if they can hold water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רבא said, and the ברייתא adds more examples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leather wineskins are made to hold liquid, so once they are prepared they work for washing. A sack and a basket are not made to hold water, so even one that happens to hold water does not count as a vessel for washing.

keyTerms.meaning: A leather wineskin
Another type of leather container for liquids
A sack and a basket
Even though they can hold (water)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that any object which holds water is fine. A sack or basket that holds water still does not count, because that kind of object is not made to hold liquids.
steps.whatToRemember: A valid vessel for washing must be the kind of thing made or prepared to hold liquid. A prepared stopper or wineskin works. A sack or basket never does.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way (in a ברייתא):
A barrel stopper that one prepared,
one may wash hands from it.
A ḥemet and a kefisha that one prepared,
phrases.notes: Both are kinds of leather containers made for holding liquids.

phrases.english: one may wash hands from them.

phrases.aramaic: שַׂק וְקוּפָּה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמְּקַבְּלִים –
phrases.english: A sack and a basket, even though they can hold (water),
one may not wash hands from them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up רבא's ruling with a ברייתא and widens the list of cases.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that a prepared barrel stopper is valid for washing
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same wording, which also covers wineskins, sacks and baskets

steps.title: May one eat with a cloth instead of washing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether someone may eat while holding food with a cloth instead of washing his hands, or whether we worry he will touch the food.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: what is the law about eating with a cloth? Do we worry that maybe he will touch the food, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question: can a cloth over the hands take the place of washing?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Washing is needed so the hands do not touch the bread while they are unwashed. If a cloth stands between the hands and the food, maybe washing is not needed. The question is whether we fear that the person will slip and touch the food with his bare hand.

keyTerms.meaning: A question that was asked, an open dilemma
A cloth or napkin
We are concerned or we worry
Perhaps he will touch (the food)

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
What is the law about eating with a cloth?
phrases.notes: He means holding the food in a cloth without washing his hands first.

phrases.english: Are we concerned that perhaps he will touch,
or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from which vessel to wash with to whether washing can be skipped by using a cloth.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether eating with a cloth can replace נטילת ידים, or whether we worry the person will touch the food.

steps.title: Trying to prove from רבי צדוק, who ate with a cloth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the case of רבי צדוק, who ate less than a כביצה with a cloth, and suggests this means a כביצה would need washing even with a cloth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: when they gave רבי צדוק food smaller than a כביצה, he took it in a cloth, ate it outside the סוכה, and did not say a ברכה after it. Doesn't this mean that a כביצה needs washing of the hands?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question from a case: רבי צדוק used a cloth only for a small amount of food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי צדוק used a cloth for less than a כביצה. The גמרא suggests that for a full כביצה, the cloth would not have been enough and he would have needed real washing. If so, a cloth does not replace washing, because we worry he may touch the food.

keyTerms.meaning: Less than the size of an egg
Outside the סוכה
He does not say a ברכה after eating it
Is it not so that...? (the start of a suggested proof)

steps.confusionAlert: The cloth is not about the סוכה or the ברכה. The small size of the food explains those two details. The cloth is the detail that relates to our question about washing.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
phrases.notes: This is from the משנה in סוכה 26b.

phrases.english: And when they gave Rabbi Tzadok
food less than an egg-bulk,
he took it in a cloth
and ate it outside the sukka,
and did not recite a blessing after it.
Is it not so
that an egg-bulk requires washing of the hands?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is reading this from the משנה: a cloth was enough only because the food was small.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, וּכְשֶׁנָּתְנוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי צָדוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question about eating with a cloth by drawing an inference from the משנה about רבי צדוק.
steps.raayaObject: That a cloth does not replace washing for a כביצה of food, because we worry he may touch it
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in סוכה about רבי צדוק eating less than a כביצה in a cloth

steps.title: The רבי צדוק case may be about סוכה and ברכה, not washing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from רבי צדוק. The reason he ate less than a כביצה may be that a כביצה needs a סוכה and a ברכה, not that a כביצה needs washing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps the point is that a כביצה needs a סוכה and needs a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is knocking down the proof from the last step. It offers another reason why רבי צדוק ate less than a כביצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 17 the גמרא thought רבי צדוק stayed below a כביצה because a כביצה would need washing even with a cloth. Now the גמרא says the size limit may be about other rules: eating a כביצה requires a סוכה and an after-blessing. So a cloth might still work in place of washing even for a כביצה, and our question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps; a word used to offer another way to read a source
The amount of an egg; an important size in many halachos
The booth one must eat in on סוכות
A blessing; here, the blessing said after eating

phrases.english: Perhaps this means that an egg-bulk
phrases.notes: He means the story of רבי צדוק from the previous step, who ate less than a כביצה.

phrases.english: needs a sukka, and needs a blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 17 by giving the רבי צדוק case another explanation.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from רבי צדוק. It does not decide the question about the cloth.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The size limit in the רבי צדוק case can be explained by the rules of סוכה and ברכה, so it does not prove that a כביצה needs washing.

steps.title: A new proof begins: שמואל finds רב eating with a cloth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new proof for the cloth question. It tells of שמואל finding רב eating with a cloth, and begins to quote what שמואל said to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: שמואל found רב eating with a cloth, and said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new proof for the cloth question. It tells the story here, and שמואל's actual words come on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the רבי צדוק proof was rejected, the גמרא looks for another source. We now know רב was eating with a cloth instead of washing his hands. The proof will depend on how שמואל reacts, which comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: He found him
That he was eating
